subject: Regional telemetry retention & replication commitments — follow-up
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Arnold <michael.arnold@praxitech.com>, DPO <dpo@praxitech.com>, Security Team <security@praxitech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:13:00 -0000
Subject: Regional telemetry retention & replication commitments — follow-up

Hi Michael / Praxitech team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per your ask, I’m capturing the current Redwood position on telemetry (operational logs, metrics, traces) retention and cross-region replication so your legal and security teams can review. Attaching a short SLA draft and our current subprocessor roster for transparency.

Summary (asks at the bottom):
- Telemetry retention by region (default):
  * EU tenants: operational telemetry retained for 14 days (short-term logs) and 90 days for aggregated metrics used for platform health.
  * US tenants: operational telemetry retained for 30 days, aggregated metrics 180 days.
  * APAC tenants: operational telemetry retained for 14 days, aggregated metrics 90 days.
- Cross-region replication:
  * Replication only to a single secondary region for failover; replication occurs asynchronously and is scoped to encrypted telemetry (no customer payloads).
  * Transient egress window for failover: up to 72 hours to restore service in the event of a regional outage. During that window telemetry may traverse a secondary region.
- Keys & encryption:
  * Customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys. For EU-specific commitments we can offer key residency with CMKs in EU regions (requires dedicated onboarding).
- Analytics exports & third-party processors:
  * We will not export raw telemetry out of the tenant region for analytics unless explicitly agreed and documented in an addendum. Aggregated metrics used for product telemetry may be stored cross-region per retention policy above.

Attachments: Telemetry_Retention_SLA_v1.pdf (short SLA), subprocessor_roster_q3_2027.csv

Asks:
1) Can you confirm Praxitech’s acceptable maximum transient egress window (we’re proposing 72 hours)?
2) Do you require an additional DPA addendum or a specific clause stating telemetry is out-of-scope for EU->US exports?
3) Any regulatory constraints that would require us to change the retention numbers above?

If helpful, Marissa from Legal and Jonas from Ops are cc’d to iterate language quickly. Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Lead — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
---

From: Michael Arnold <michael.arnold@praxitech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@praxitech.com>, DPO <dpo@praxitech.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 13:41:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Regional telemetry retention & replication commitments — follow-up

Kimberly — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side after an initial pass:

- 72 hours for transient egress is likely at the upper bound of what we can accept for EU-regulated customers. For our EU product lines we’d prefer 48 hours or less. Can Redwood confirm you can SLA 48h for EU-only tenants?
- We need explicit language that raw telemetry containing request/response metadata that can be used to reconstruct user activity will never be exported outside the tenant region without prior written consent. Aggregated metrics are fine, but we need that hard boundary in the DPA addendum.
- SOC 2 / audit evidence: our auditors will want a short packet showing the replication controls, KMS key residency proof, and a copy of any contractual addendum.

I’m attaching (inlined) a short checklist the security team put together. Can Marissa or your contracts team propose wording for the two bullets above so our legal can speed review?

Thanks —
Michael
Michael Arnold
Head of IT Security
Praxitech Ltd.
security@praxitech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Arnold <michael.arnold@praxitech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 16:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Regional telemetry retention & replication commitments — follow-up

Hi Michael — looping in operations to confirm feasibility and proposing draft language below that we can put into a DPA addendum / SLA. Jonas, can you confirm ops can meet the EU 48-hour transient egress window if we commit that in writing for EU-only tenants? If not, please propose the operational mitigations.

Proposed contract language (high level):
1) Telemetry export restriction: "Redwood Inference will not transfer raw operational telemetry (logs, request/response metadata, traces) that could be used to reconstruct user activity outside the tenant's designated region without the tenant's prior written consent. Aggregated or anonymized metrics intended for platform health and product analytics are excluded from this restriction and may be replicated cross-region per the retention schedule."
2) Transient failover window: "In the event of a qualified regional outage, Redwood may replicate/serve telemetry from a designated secondary region for the minimum period necessary to restore service, not to exceed 48 hours for tenants with EU residency commitments. Redwood will log and provide audit evidence of any transient cross-region processing and notify the tenant within 2 hours of failover initiation."
3) KMS residency: "For customers with Dedicated or Private deployments, customer-managed keys (CMKs) can be provisioned in the tenant region. Hosted customers may request CMK support; additional onboarding fees may apply."

Jonas: operational notes? We can start with this text and I’ll circulate a redline addendum. Michael — once we have ops confirmation I’ll put this into the DPA addendum template and send a DocuSign link.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Counsel
Redwood Inference
